story.headline: A graduate study finds a tougher start in AI-exposed majors.

heroVisual.alt: An illustrated laptop, blank application tracker and application papers on a desk.

story.the_story:
A September working paper by Census Bureau researchers follows bachelor’s graduates from 2016–2024 at participating US institutions—about 29% of degrees in those years. Employment records run through September 2025.

“AI exposure” estimates how much AI could help with tasks in occupations associated with a major. It does not count jobs AI actually replaced.
story.laidies_read:
After ChatGPT arrived, the most-exposed tenth of majors—largely computing—had about five percentage points lower employment in the quarter after graduation relative to the least-exposed 60%, after accounting for their 2022 difference.

For the arithmetic alone, a move from 80% to 75% is five percentage points. That is a 6.25% relative decrease. These illustrative rates are not the study’s starting employment rates. “Five points” and “five percent” answer different questions.

Initial earnings were about 13% lower in the main full-quarter job—a job spanning the whole quarter—two quarters after graduation. That is a group comparison, not an annual pay cut for every graduate.

The authors argue AI played an important role. They cannot rule out coinciding field-specific changes. Their employment records omit self-employment and graduate school; the college sample is not nationally representative.

Author conclusions are not Census endorsements; this working paper has not undergone the review given Census publications. Independent replication is not established here.
story.what_this_means:
Picture a graduate and parent looking at a spreadsheet of unanswered applications. The useful question is not “Is this degree finished?” It is “What first jobs are recent graduates in this subject actually finding, and how long did that take?” Ask the career office for the group, time window and destinations behind its answer.

A difficult search deserves practical help without a diagnosis invented from a headline. Use the study to sharpen that conversation, rather than turn a group average into a verdict on one person’s prospects. It supplies no demonstrated remedy of switching majors.
story.cocktail_party: “Worse relative graduate outcomes are evidence of pressure, not a personal diagnosis.”
story.class_notes: Read a result by asking who was counted, what was compared and what was left out.

universalAnswers.whatHappened: September2026 working paper reports worsening relative entry outcomes afterChatGPT for most-exposed majors.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A study follows bachelor graduates into measured employment instead of inferring exposure from their eventual job.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Complete79page primaryPDF captured; maintext inspected; author limitations retained.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Observational, selectedinstitutions, missing activities; no proof AI caused each outcome or all unemployment.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Graduates and parents need a useful question rather than a degree-doom inference.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: Bachelor graduates in sampledUSinstitutions; most-exposed group largelycomputing, no women-specificresult claimed.
universalAnswers.changesNow: New bounded research evidence; no forecast or policy change asserted.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Independent replication not verified, permanentcareer consequences unresolved, coinciding field changes cannot be excluded.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Ask career office about actual firstjob destinations and searchduration for comparable graduates.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Which graduates, employment window and destinations underlie a headline or career-office answer?

research-benchmark.result: Aboutfivepoint initialemployment relative decline and13% lower mainfullquarter initial earnings attwoquarters; no disputedtwo-yearmetric.
research-benchmark.sponsorAndInterests: Census researchers CodyOrr, LeeTucker, LawrenceWarren; author conclusions notofficialendorsement. LEHDdata program partlyNSF/NIA/Sloansupported; no vendorinterest documented.
research-benchmark.independentReplication: No independent replication verified; article states workingpaper review status without implyingpeerreview.
research-benchmark.realWorldTransfer: Actual record evidence about selected graduate groups; cannotdiagnose one application spreadsheet or provechangingmajors helps.
research-benchmark.limitations: Selected institutions, non-wage activities omitted, coinciding field shocks; exposure estimates capability not adoption.
